A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that VEGFR3 is a promising target for the suppression of lymphangiogenesis, and that this is associated with a reduction in tumor lymphatic vessel density, and consequently a reduction in the number of metastases in the regional lymph nodes.

the VEGFR-3 signaling axis is a crucial regulator of lymphatic endothelial cell (LEC) proliferation, migration, and lymphangiogenesis, and that the inhibition of this axis may be an attractive therapeutic target for the prevention and treatment of metastasis and lymphedema.

we have identified a new role for VEGF-C/VEGFR3 signaling in tumor lymphangiogenesis in vivo and that this pathway is a target for anti-lymphangiogenic therapy.
